content: I'll start by reading the test image to identify the key visual features.

The test image shows two banana fruits on a white background. Key observations:
- **Bottom banana**: Severely affected — orange/yellowish skin with large, dark brown-to-black irregular blotches/lesions covering a significant portion of the fruit surface. The tip (distal end) appears darkened and shriveled.
- **Top banana**: Green with some yellowish areas and scattered small dark spots.
- Affected part: **Fruit/pod** (not leaf, stem, or root)
- The dark, sunken-looking lesions on the fruit, especially at the tip, are characteristic.

The dark tip and lesions on the fruit strongly suggest **Cigar End Rot** (which causes darkening and drying of the distal end) or **Anthracnose** (which causes dark post-harvest lesions on fruit). Let me check reference images from these two classes first, then explore others.
Cigar End Rot shows blackened/shriveled tip (distal end). The test image has more widespread dark blotches across the whole fruit surface rather than just the tip. Let me check Anthracnose next.
Excellent match! Anthracnose shows widespread dark brown-to-black irregular blotches on banana fruit, very similar to the test image. Let me check one more class to be thorough.
Panama Disease affects leaves with yellowing, not fruit with dark blotches. My 4th view should cover one more class for completeness.

Cordana Leaf Spot shows dark spots on leaves — clearly a leaf disease, not matching the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Class | Reference observed | Match to test image |
|---|---|---|
| **Anthracnose** | PlantWild_26.jpg | **Strong match** — widespread dark brown-black irregular blotches across fruit surface |
| Cigar_End_Rot | PlantWild_27.jpg | Poor — only tip blackening, rest of fruit healthy |
| Panama_Disease | Banana_Leaf_1006.jpg | Poor — leaf yellowing, not fruit lesions |
| Cordana_Leaf_Spot | Banana_Leaf_136.jpeg | Poor — dark spots on leaves, not fruit |

The test image shows two banana fruits with large, irregular, coalescing dark brown-to-black lesions spread across the fruit surface (especially the bottom fruit), which is the hallmark of **Anthracnose** caused by *Colletotrichum musae*. The tip darkening also aligns. This pattern was clearly confirmed by the Anthracnose reference image showing identical widespread blotchy lesions on banana fruits.
